title: TypeError: this.attributes.position is undefined
ruled_out_findings: InstancedBufferGeometry for a million position-less points shows no speed advantage over the drawRange/groups approach
summary: Rendering points without a position attribute; drawRange/groups handling reworked. Measurement showed instanced vs non-instanced position-less points perform identically.

title: CSS3DRenderer.js not packaged with three.js?
summary: Question about why CSS3DRenderer ships in examples/ rather than the core build; a passing aside asks whether there are performance problems but none are discussed.

title: Vector Equals with Tolerance
summary: Proposal to add a tolerance argument to Vector.equals(); discussion notes the extra conditional/branch and that distanceTo (sqrt) is slower than a manhattan-style comparison. Closed without change.
evidence: makc: "I use .distanceTo but this would be faster... probably"

title: Three.js performance compared to asm.js/wasm ports.
summary: Open-ended question comparing three.js to asm.js/wasm engine ports; maintainer says the demo could run at 60fps in three.js, but no mechanism of cost is identified.

title: Performance: Multiple tiny sprites
summary: 200-1500 tiny text sprites halved FPS. Root cause: WebGLRenderer was not frustum-culling Sprites, so off-screen sprites still issued draw calls. Fixed by mrdoob.
evidence: mrdoob: "turns out `WebGLRenderer` was not frustum culling Sprites!" || Nefsen402: "The problem here is most likely all the draw calls."

title: Threejs garbage collection behaviour
ruled_out_findings: Setting render-list length to 0 each frame would force reallocating all render-list entry objects every frame, which is why the cache is kept
summary: Disposed meshes stay in the heap unless an extra render() happens: the renderer's opaqueObjects/transparentObjects arrays keep references, deliberately not truncated (length = writeIndex+1) to avoid per-frame reallocation. Accepted as a perf tradeoff; DOM event handlers on the canvas also retain the renderer.
evidence: mrdoob: "the browser won't be able to remove the references with the `opaqueObjects.length = opaqueObjectsLastIndex + 1` optimisation"; "So the reported issue is a price we have to pay for performance." || tschw: "At some point it occurred to me that is must be the event handlers, of course" (earlier: "But I'm not really sure why it's needed.")

title: Further improvements to MeshPhysicalMaterial
ruled_out_findings: Single-image cubemaps may give better performance when generating LOD levels than six-face cubemaps
summary: Roadmap of MeshPhysicalMaterial improvements. Perf-relevant: textureCubeLodEXT-based roughness LOD lookup is out-of-spec/unsupported on many devices, auto mipmap generation quality vs. cost, and cost of generating full LOD pyramids for live light probes.
evidence: bhouston: "This requires fast filtering and maybe necessary to use HW cube map generation or we can just not do LOD"

title: WebGL-based Prefiltered Mipmaped Radiance Environment Map (PMREM) generator
summary: Request for a GPU-based PMREM generator because the offline AMD CubeMapGen tool is too slow; discussion analyses filtering cost (NxM level generation, separable vs single-shot filters, 49 vs 14 samples) and implementation-limit tradeoffs.
evidence: body: "We can use this tool to create them off line, but it is very inconvenient also this tool is slow:" || tschw: "generating NxM levels is relatively expensive"

title: Comment animation mixed example code
summary: Request for comments in animation examples. Maintainer notes the r73 examples contain obsolete manual optimizations and that the rewritten dev animation system is several times faster; AnimationObjectGroup is mentioned as an optimization.

title: NodeMaterial
summary: Long NodeMaterial design/enhancement thread: architecture, naming, node types, editors, serialization, and whether it belongs in src/. Performance appears only in asides — node graph build/runtime cost with TempNode caching, callback-based array iteration being slower than explicit loops, and unclean alpha-return emulation of discard. None measured.
evidence: sunag: "how much more nodes this consumes more CPU at build time and GPU at runtime" || bhouston: "Function calls are very slow in JavaScript compared to a for-loop or while-loop"

title: getNormalMatrix(), getInverse() aren't getters
summary: Naming debate about getNormalMatrix()/getInverse(); an aside asserts that combined copy+invert methods are faster than copy().invert() and that avoiding overloading helps the V8 JIT.

title: self in three.js is bound to the wrong Variable if "var self = this;" is used in the calling context
summary: Clock.getDelta() broke because app code overwrote the global `self`, so `self.performance` was undefined. Turned out to be app-side misuse of `var self = this`; the `performance` token is incidental.

title: requestAnimationFrame loop causes CPU hog
summary: Unconditional requestAnimationFrame render loop keeps rendering a static scene every 16ms, pegging a CPU core; maintainers say on-demand rendering is the app's responsibility, and dirty-tracking in the engine would itself cost performance.
evidence: benbucksch: "The CPU usage drops from 2 cores with 100% each to almost nothing, after 2 seconds of no activity on my page."

title: Add light source radius to point and spot lights to enable accurate soft shadows?
summary: Feature request to add light source radius to enable PCSS soft shadows; resolved by adding radius to light.shadow. Performance is only tangential.

title: SpotLight should automatically update LightShadow camera in response to SpotLight parameter changes
summary: Request to auto-couple SpotLight.angle to its shadow camera fov. Discussion notes that a loose shadow frustum wastes shadow-map resolution, and that recomputing the projection matrix in render() each frame would cost cycles; implemented via SpotLightShadow which only recomputes when values change.
evidence: WestLangley: "I think a common user requirement is to have the shadow frustum tight around the target for better-quality shadows at lower cost" — hedged with "I think" and disputed by bhouston || MasterJames: "in the render function might not be the most performant place to update"; mrdoob notes update() "only computes the projectionMatrix if the values are different" — no measurement

title: Versioning !
summary: Complaint about API churn/migration burden across versions. Only performance-adjacent content is the note that ShaderMaterial custom attributes were removed in favour of BufferGeometry attributes for performance reasons.

title: Fog doesn't work on Chrome in Nexus devices if antialias = true
summary: Fog is pushed far back on Adreno/Qualcomm Android GPUs when antialias=true, due to a wrong gl_FragCoord.w in the driver (Qualcomm bug filed, WebGL conformance test added). Workaround of disabling AA plus doubling pixelRatio is noted as costing performance.

title: computeBoundingBox not called in mesh.raycast
ruled_out_findings: Transforming the single ray into model space is cheaper than transforming all vertices into world space, so raycast uses the inverse matrix approach || Bounding-box prefilter adds a matrix inverse per raycast that may only pay off for some models, so only the bounding sphere is tested
summary: Question about why Mesh.raycast doesn't auto-compute a bounding box and why ray-vs-box is done in model space; maintainer explains transforming one ray into model space is cheaper than transforming all vertices to world space, and bounding-box prefiltering may or may not pay off depending on the model.

title: Raycaster in r73 not working correctly with MultiMaterial objects
ruled_out_findings: Raycaster intentionally dropped per-face multi-material resolution; it was a design/perf tradeoff rather than a measured hotspot
summary: Raycaster no longer respects MultiMaterial per-face materials; maintainer states this was dropped deliberately for simplicity and performance, and recommends splitting geometry.

title: AnimationMixer AnimationClip, AnimationAction missing in doc
summary: Request for docs on the animation system; mentions of performance are incidental (example filename webgl_shadowmap_performance, aside that new mixer caches).

title: Group materialIndex ignored when converting groups to faces in Geometry.fromBufferGeometry
summary: Geometry.fromBufferGeometry ignores group materialIndex; discussion notes Geometry is converted to BufferGeometry before render, costing time and memory.

title: Sprite issues
summary: Sprite API limitations; cloning textures per-sprite causes repeated GPU uploads, and the uuid hack causes image decode stalls.
evidence: WestLangley: "Confirmed." ... "prevents the texture from being uploaded to the GPU repeatedly."

title: Android Chrome Dev still a problem with WebGL video textures
summary: Android Chrome video texture rendering broken/slow on Samsung S3; traced to a Chromium media pipeline bug and old GPU hardware.
evidence: Enabling the "unified media pipeline" flag in Chrome Dev fixes rendering of three.js video textures but then it produces a problem of cpu performance problems. || danrossi: "older models like the S3 is too laggy to use for video texture WebGL rendering. It still causes underlying video playback and performance issues with dropped frames."

title: Image distortion
summary: Image distortion/jerky rotation on a textured cube; redirected to StackOverflow, no mechanism established.

title: Why does aoMap only use the red channel?
summary: Discussion of why aoMap uses only the red channel; performance mentioned only as an aside, decision was semantic.

title: Geometry.verticesNeedUpdate seems doesn't work correctly
summary: verticesNeedUpdate not working due to cached __directGeometry; deleting the cache works but is slow.
evidence: airycanon: "When I deleted `geometry.__directGeometry`,the geometry did update,but the `rendering performance` dropped down"

title: Viewports && scissors && canvas background protection enhancement
summary: Question about viewports/scissors and transparent canvas background; asks whether alpha:true hurts performance but no answer or mechanism given.

title: Recommendation: Constructors taking JSON
summary: Proposal for JSON-object constructors; performance mentioned only as passing speculation, rejected by maintainer.

title: Custom UVs on standard Geometry
summary: Request for saving custom UVs on parametric geometries; CPU cost mentioned only in passing with no issue observed.

title: Suggestion: Javascript Binary Bundles for faster loading and distribution
summary: Proposal for a binary bundle format (JBB) claiming ~30% faster asset load vs JSON loaders; benchmarks disputed on fast connections; closed with redirect to forum.
evidence: wavesoft: "I observe an average loading time improvement of about **30%**" || wavesoft: "you will end-up with dozens of faces/vertices/indices, while you could just encode the constructor parameters (optimising for size)"

title: Group seems not work correctly in editor
summary: Editor group re-parenting question; closed as duplicate of #7532. A comment mentions the parent select box was removed 'for performance reasons' without detail.

title: Safari/Firefox DOM Exception 18 for Streaming Video Texture
summary: Cross-origin video textures throw DOM Exception 18 in Safari/iOS due to missing WebKit CORS support for video (fixed in iOS 11.1); workarounds include reverse-proxy, iframe, or Cordova WebView. Performance appears as side remarks: canvas 2D drawImage intermediate drops frames, and older iOS devices render WebGL at ~5fps.
evidence: danrossi: "I wouldn't even use canvas drawing that will drop too many frames." || danrossi: "The Ipad 3 is useless for WebGL and renders back at 5fps."

title: Clock (start, getDelta) broken in Node.js r74, 'performance.now' not defined
summary: THREE.Clock breaks in Node/iOS8 because performance.now polyfill was removed; discussion of timing APIs, not a performance cost.

title: TrackballControls is much slower than its older version
summary: Claim that new TrackballControls is slower than the old one; reporter later could not reproduce, attributed to slower rotation speed perception. No mechanism established.

title: webgl_shadowmap_performance.html halves FPS r74 vs r73
summary: FPS halved in webgl_shadowmap_performance between r73 and r74; traced to the rewritten PCFSoftShadowMap being more expensive (higher quality) — removing that setting restored 55-60fps.
evidence: izatar: "my framerate shoots up to 55-60" after removing `renderer.shadowMap.type = THREE.PCFSoftShadowMap;`; mrdoob: "Yes, that makes sense. `PCFSoftShadowMap` has more quality now."

title: render targets small resolution on postprocessing
summary: EffectComposer render targets ignore devicePixelRatio, giving blurry postprocessing; setting full-DPR size fixes quality but halves FPS due to 4x fragment work.
evidence: "it works like a charm and everything is crisp as butter at only half the FPS"

title: Undeclared identifier 'IncidentLight' on Windows
summary: Shader compile failure 'undeclared identifier IncidentLight' on ANGLE D3D9 path (Quadro 600 / AMD switchable graphics fallback); driver/ANGLE compiler bug with struct-returning functions, worked around by using out parameters.

title: OBJLoader + MTLLoader != OBJMTLLoader
summary: OBJLoader lacks OBJMTLLoader features (mtllib, multi-material per mesh). Discussion of whether splitting into child meshes vs BufferGeometry groups/MultiMaterial has different draw-call overhead; concluded groups approach preserves file structure but still produces multiple draw calls.
evidence: jonnenauha: "Just multiple materials with group indexing that will produce multiple draw calls." || jonnenauha: "I guess we should not mark the index except when multiple materials are encountered, to not put any overhead or make all obj loading create groups and user multimaterial when not needed."

title: Saw-tooth memory profile / leak (particularly bad with MeshStandardMaterial)
ruled_out_findings: Sawtooth heap profile comes from Chrome's own dynamic memory for internal bookkeeping/JIT optimization, not three.js per-frame allocations (verified by recording heap allocations over a selected timef
summary: Reported saw-tooth memory profile/GC churn in three.js examples, initially attributed to material uniforms. Maintainer profiling showed no allocations from three.js code; sawtooth comes from Chrome's internal bookkeeping, though TextGeometry (non-buffer) inflated allocation in one example.
evidence: tschw: "The 10MB in `webgl_materials_variations_standard` become 1MB without `TextGeometry`" || tschw: "there should be no allocation required, unless the number of rendered objects varies due to culling"

title: Proposal: Bring Back Shadow Intensity (formerly Shadow Darkness)
summary: Proposal for shadow intensity/darkness property. Mostly a rendering-feature discussion; one commenter asserts that the extra-lights workaround costs performance, and mrdoob notes it adds one uniform per light.

title: Request for Feature: Screen Space Reflections
summary: Feature request for screen-space reflections. Prototype passes are heavily resolution-dependent (4-5 fps at 1080p) because ray marching runs per full-resolution pixel for every fragment regardless of reflectivity; also a material was created every render call.
evidence: WestLangley: "the frame rate is 4"; gkjohnson: "It's a very resolution-dependent effect so if you make your window smaller the framerate will probably go up" || Fyrestar: "Did you noticed you create a material in each render call?" || gkjohnson: "though ray tracing is still happening so there won't be any performance difference in that case"

title: iOS performance issue
summary: iOS 9 / iPhone 6 stalls every second in a simple scene while FPS stays at 60; no mechanism identified, redirected to forum.

title: three.clock uses window.performance and does not work on IOS 8
summary: THREE.Clock used window.performance, which Apple disabled on iOS 8 due to performance issues in the Navigation Timing API, breaking projects; fixed in dev by falling back to Date.

title: Request for Object3D method to assign (replace) children by array index (updated first post)
summary: Request for Object3D.replaceChildAt/replace to avoid indexOf search and splice when swapping children; closed by reporter as low value.
evidence: "In addition to the (at least theoretical) performance advantages" and "saves a splice, and if the application developer knows the index of the element to replace, then using that information with replaceAt will save a search too."

title: Is Geometry.elementsNeedUpdate deprecated in r74
summary: Geometry.elementsNeedUpdate was non-functional, then after the fix was never reset to false, causing DirectGeometry to be rebuilt every frame.
evidence: sylvain-abadie: "geometry.elementsNeedUpdate is never set back to false.  This leads to a massive performance and memory issue :  DirectGeometries keep getting instantiated."

title: Three.js Cardboard effect performance issues
summary: CardboardEffect's render-to-texture then redraw of a distorted plane costs a full extra fullscreen pixel pass on high-DPI phones; vertex-displacement distortion proposed and measured faster. CardboardEffect removed.
evidence: body: "I presume this is because the pixels are effectively being drawn twice"

title: Some glTF scenes slow performance significantly when used with VREffect
summary: glTFShaders.update() calls scene.updateMatrixWorld() once per shader every frame, dropping to ~2fps on large glTF scenes.
evidence: donmccurdy: "It's invoked once per shader." || tparisi: "I'm not keeping track of whether or not values have changed since the last frame"

title: Unexpected result from calling Box3.setFromObject() on transformed mesh
summary: Box3.setFromObject was changed to traverse all geometry vertices for accuracy, which is far slower than unioning child bounding boxes; users doing per-frame AABB updates for octree/picking lost their frame rate.
evidence: brianchirls: "is crawling through the whole geometry anyway" || brianchirls: "traversing every single triangle of every moving object on every frame"

title: PBR Light Limits
summary: Adding >12 shadow-casting point lights exceeds MAX_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS since each shadow-casting light consumes a fragment shader sampler.
evidence: body: "Fragment shader sampler count exceeds MAX_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS (16)."

title: Clipping planes
summary: Request for built-in clipping planes, including using them in frustum culling; three.js added clipping in #8465 with global planes culled but local planes not.
evidence: tschw: "The global clipping state _is_ considered during frustum culling. The local one is seen as a modeling operation and thus is not."

title: THREE.Audio: .load has been deprecated. Please use THREE.AudioLoader.
summary: Complaint about deprecation of THREE.Audio.load in favour of THREE.AudioLoader; only an offhand aside that 'good looking code = bad performances'.

title: PR Proposal: Program input data sources
summary: Proposal for a declarative program input linkage table to replace hard-coded renderer uniform/define wiring. Perf arguments: renderState defines recomputed per material, imperative per-object callbacks must evaluate all dependency checks per object, and declarative tables would enable WebGL2 uniform blocks to cut API calls. Closed without adoption; no measurements.
evidence: bhouston: "renderState defines are recomputed for each material, when really they could be computed once and shared between all materials" || tschw: "Running a nested call hierarchy doing lots of redundant stuff there, may not make it just _slightly_ slower." || tschw: "it allows to very effectively utilize uniform blocks become available with WebGL2 to reduce API calls and the amount of data uploaded to the GPU" || tschw: "we actually had quirky workarounds it in some of the examples in `r73` in order to use the new animation system - it was too slow"

title: error of DirectGeometry
summary: BufferGeometry.fromGeometry()/DirectGeometry produces non-indexed geometry, duplicating vertices (e.g. 774 -> 4095 positions), causing large FPS drops; maintainers say it's by design since indexed conversion can't support needsUpdate.
evidence: "my build: 45 fps (rotating) / 60 fps (still)" vs "current r84: 20 fps (rotating) / 35 fps (still)"; also "774 positions and seeing the number go up to 4095 positions after `.fromGeometry()`"

title: Proposal: Making flattened math classes that operate directly on views the default
summary: Proposal to rewrite math classes over flat typed-array views to avoid per-object allocation/GC and copy costs; prototype PRs showed no speedup and the issue was closed as outdated.
evidence: body: "It has a large overhead per object in terms of allocation time and extra memory usage because it is an editable object.  There are also costs to copy from a BufferGeometry array to a Vector3 and vice " || greggman: "`Float32Array` is slow. I'm only guessing it's because there is a required conversion to/from 64bit doubles"

title: Custom Shaders in r76
summary: Custom skinning shader broke in r76 because the uniform boneGlobalMatrices was renamed to boneMatrices; perf only mentioned in passing.

title: Replace THREE.Cache by localForage for mobile support
summary: Request to replace THREE.Cache with localForage for persistent asset caching; rejected as out of scope, with anecdotal reports that IndexedDB blob storage was slower than re-fetch+parse.
evidence: "it was slooow to save and load back. Was much faster to load from browser cache and load/parse to geom." and "Could take 200msec and the next page load takes 800ms for the same data"

title: Vertex Array Objects (VAO) usage in THREE.
summary: Request for VAO support to reduce per-draw attribute binding API calls; cited 10-13% FPS gain in CPU-bound tests, eventually implemented.
evidence: Mugen87 quoting WebGL Insights: "In our CPU-bound drawing test, FPS increase from using VAOs was 10%-13%"

title: Shadowmap regression in r76?
summary: Shadow map visual regression in r76 traced to a shadow bias default change; reporter's separate FPS drop turned out to be caused by using Chrome Canary, no mechanism identified.

title: Fast Polygon Lights (would include Area)
summary: Proposal to add LTC-based polygonal/area lights. Long implementation thread; performance concerns raised about float texture extensions, per-fragment integration cost on mobile, and RGBA-packed float decoding being slow.
evidence: bhouston: "There is existing code in ThreeJS to pack/unpack a fp32 into a RGBA8, but it is slow." || bhouston: "I think that for mobile you really do want to cache what you can because glsl compute shader capacity is greatly limited."

title: vertex cache optimisation
ruled_out_findings: Scenes are fragment-shader bound rather than vertex bound, so vertex cache ordering yields little benefit
summary: Suggestion to add Forsyth vertex-cache triangle-order optimisation utility. Maintainers argue three.js apps are fragment-bound, not vertex-bound; later noted meshoptimizer/gltfpack does this offline.
evidence: body quote: "If the triangles are sent in a random order, the vertices almost always miss the cache and there is no benefit obtained."

title: IQ's fast stereo rendering article
summary: Request to adopt IQ's single-pass stereo rendering. Discussion identifies duplicated frustum culling and render-list building per eye, and shader program state changes as the dominant cost. Closed once ArrayCamera landed.
evidence: For a "random" array of cameras we'd have to do frustum culling individually and duplicate all render items. || tschw: "showing programs to be the most expensive ones by far"

title: Addressing ThreeJS's load time: smaller meshes = faster loader (OpenCTM 2?)
summary: Proposal for a better compressed mesh format; asserts three.js binary format is 2-5x larger than OpenCTM gzipped, dominating load/start-up time. Discussion of Open3DGC, SEA3D, Draco.
evidence: "We have found on average that OpenCTM meshes are 2x to 5x smaller than ThreeJS's binary format gzipped"; sunag: "The `robot.sea` with 1.107MB now + Open3DGC only 652kB" || "OBJ, JSON, DAE and all the other TEXT files are not suitable for online projects."

title: maybe add callback check to AnimationMixer.js
summary: Request to add a direct callback instead of an EventDispatcher event on animation finish, claiming it is more performant. Maintainer says event dispatch overhead is negligible here.

title: Object3D new viewable property
summary: Request to cache frustum-culling results on Object3D as a `viewable` flag to avoid redoing per-object frustum tests; maintainer proposed a standalone camera.isInView() helper instead, calling the caching a premature optimisation. Reporter benchmarked both variants and confirmed the batched version (recomputing frustum/matrix once per call rather than per object) is measurably faster.
evidence: verteAzur: "We can see a true performance gain with your latest function."

title: Temporal Anti Aliasing (TAA) rounding errors over accumulation
ruled_out_findings: 8-bit render targets were chosen over half/float for TAA accumulation partly for performance and memory (2-4x lower), causing rounding/quantization artifacts
summary: TAARenderPass accumulation darkens frames due to incorrect per-frame sample weighting/8-bit rounding. Side discussion establishes why 8-bit render targets were chosen over half/float: compatibility, performance and 2-4x lower memory.

title: Shadow Updates And Normal Maps
summary: After the shadow refactor, normal-mapped surfaces in shadow look flat; the suggested workaround is to add a HemisphereLight, which the reporter says costs performance. No measurement or confirmation of that cost.
evidence: titansoftime: "The additional light comes at a performance cost"

title: Faster Vector3.prototype.projectOnVector
summary: Vector3.projectOnVector allocated a closure temp Vector3 and called normalize()+extra function calls; rewriting to use dot/lengthSq was benchmarked ~30% faster and merged via #9101.
evidence: "My version: 486 ms" ... "Current version: 705 ms"

title: Logarithmic Depth Buffer + Orthographic Camera
summary: logarithmicDepthBuffer produced z-fighting with OrthographicCamera; fixed by detecting a perspective projection matrix in the shader. Discussion notes that using #defines instead would require recompiling all materials whenever the camera type changes, which is prohibitive for multi-viewport apps.
evidence: josefri: "Recompiling wouldn't be an option, it took to long since we are using the same scene graph for all view ports"

title: Firefox Nightly: Error: WebGL: texImage2D: Chosen format/type incured an expensive reformat: 0x1908/0x1401
summary: Firefox logs "texImage2D: Chosen format/type incured an expensive reformat" for all three.js textures: the browser must do a CPU-side pixel conversion because the source image is BGRX8 while the requested destination format is RGBA8, plus UNPACK_FLIP_Y_WEBGL forces conversion.
evidence: peppsac: "$14 = mozilla::WebGLTexelFormat::BGRX8"

title: Reuse material inside THREE.EdgesHelper
ruled_out_findings: Duplicate material instances do not multiply shader programs — WebGLRenderer only creates one program for equivalent materials, so per-instance materials cost only CPU-side objects
summary: User asked to share one LineBasicMaterial across many EdgesHelper instances for performance; maintainers clarified that duplicate material instances with identical defines still map to a single WebGLProgram, so the win is only reduced CPU-side material objects, not fewer shader programs.
evidence: WestLangley: "there will be many material instances created on the CPU, so perhaps your mods can increase performance somewhat"

title: Materials with same definitions should not result in separate programs in renderer...
summary: Claim that identical materials create duplicate WebGLPrograms turned out to be user error: needsUpdate was set on only one material after setting texture.encoding, so one shader got an extra encoding prefix in prefixFragment and thus a different program. No bug.
evidence: WestLangley: "Hence, one shader had the extra prefix, and the other did not."

title: Showcase: Three.js based voxel editor
summary: Showcase of a three.js voxel editor. Author mentions capping canvas size because unoptimised rendering of >1,000,000 voxels would perform poorly.

title: Energy conservation for BlinnPhong Material
summary: Request to add energy conservation to BlinnPhong; closed wontfix because it would make the Phong shader more complex and slower, defeating its role as a cheap material.

title: Shared InterleavedBuffer and update of buffers
summary: Reporter claims a shared InterleavedBuffer across many geometries is re-uploaded once per object because WebGLRenderer compares geometry.id; maintainer says WebGLAttributes dedupes uploads and closed for lack of repro.

title: Disable lights based on object distance
summary: Proposal to enable only nearby lights per object; maintainer notes changing light counts triggers shader recompilation, which can be expensive.
evidence: mrdoob: "the shaders need to be recompiled when lights change" || body: "all data for each light is sent to GPU for each object we are rendering"

title: Support for MTL map_Ns (shininess map)
summary: Request for shininessMap on MeshPhongMaterial; long design discussion. Perf appears only as claims about Phong being (or not being) cheaper than Standard.

title: Performance and memory issue : geometry.elementsNeedUpdate is never set back to false
summary: geometry.elementsNeedUpdate was never reset to false, causing index buffers to be re-uploaded every frame; fixed by commit 723979c.
evidence: body: "geometry.elementsNeedUpdate is never set back to false"

title: matrix multilication
summary: Request for Matrix3.multiply; author benchmarked two implementations, finding the version without local variable declarations marginally faster. Withdrawn.
evidence: loldrup: "seems to be slightly faster"

title: Face visibility based on attribute value support
summary: User merged thousands of meshes into one to cut draw calls and asks for per-face visibility attribute; discussion of draw-call cost of multimaterial groups vs fragment discard.

title: overbright colors not mentioned in documentation
summary: Documentation discussion on overbright THREE.Color values; performance mentioned only as an aside about adding range-validation code.

title: IOS Ipad 3 Performance Problems Dropping Frames
summary: Low FPS playing video texture on iPad 3 / older Android; profiling showed WebGLRenderer <1ms per frame, so cost lies in video decode/texture upload on old hardware and a stale WebKit bug.
evidence: mrdoob: "`WebGLRenderer` takes less than 1ms per frame so not much that can be done there."

title: Map repeat affecting other textures' repeat on material
summary: Request for per-texture offset/repeat; concern raised that independent UV transforms would consume extra uniform/varying slots and per-vertex computation.
evidence: brianchirls: "it could take up a lot of uniform and varying slots, which might be a problem for certain GPUs if we bump up against those hardware limits"

title: setPixelRatio scales the viewport on iPad
summary: setPixelRatio (which calls setSize) scales the WebGL canvas viewport on iOS Safari; reporter was lowering pixel ratio to recover perf. Root cause is a WebKit bug (canvas.style size ignored for webgl context). Side discussions: shadows and multiple lights costing frame time; rendering on rAF vs on-demand.
evidence: mrdoob: "No matter what you set in `canvas.style.width` and `canvas.style.height` the element is always rendered with the `canvas.width` and `canvas.height` dimensions." || GianlucaGuarini: "removing the shadow has speed up ~5x the rendering" || mrdoob: "4 light sources is a lot of light sources." || michaelitvin: "rendering was done inside requestAnimationFrame"

title: Issue with MeshStandardMaterial
summary: MeshStandardMaterial artifacts on iOS at low roughness, traced to 'lowp' shader precision; the fix (forcing highp) is said to cost performance. Closed as duplicate of #9515.

title: Proposed addition to animationMixer to trigger side-effects on update.
summary: Request for an onUpdate callback on AnimationAction to avoid per-frame work or event dispatch; maintainer says event dispatch/per-frame projection matrix update is negligible. Resolved with a monkey-patch workaround.
evidence: pontiffpublishing: "conservative, among the three, of system resources"

title: MeshStandardMaterial artifacts on many mediump devices since March 2016 (Nexus 5, Samsung Galaxy.)
summary: MeshStandardMaterial precision artifacts on mediump Android devices; the known workaround of forcing highp is stated to impose a performance cost. Partially fixed later.

title: Garbage collection pauses on Firefox
summary: Firefox profiling shows WebGLRenderer's per-frame render-list sorting (Array.prototype.sort with comparator) allocates memory each frame, causing minor/incremental GC pauses (~10ms) and jank.
evidence: "some Incremental GC events are triggered which last 10ms on my machine" and profiler "showing the render's sort linked above as the primary allocation site" || "It seems like we could implement our own sorting algorithm"; "The sorted render also feels more janky than the unsorted."

title: Possibilities to optimize the rendering
summary: User asks how to speed up rendering of 150-200k vertex scenes at 30-35 FPS; advice given about polycount, object count, matrix auto-update, and hitching when new objects first render. Redirected to forum.

evidence: "I saw this little gem contribute to about 35% of GC overhead in my application or around 1kb per frame"

title: Slower OutlinePass starting in r116
ruled_out_findings: Firefox-specific rendering behaviour; maintainers saw no FPS difference in the official example
summary: Reporter observes OutlinePass slowdown from r116 in Firefox; maintainers cannot reproduce in official example and suggest a Firefox-specific issue. Left unconfirmed.

title: NodeJS support
summary: Request for official Node.js support/build of three.js; resolved by an external `three-universal` package. Discussion is about DOM globals and bundling, not performance.

title: [124] TiltLoader breaks in a module env
summary: TiltLoader breaks in module environments due to JSZip import; discussion leads to replacing JSZip/zlib.js with fflate, asserted to be much smaller (~5kB vs 80kB), faster at decompression, and more memory-efficient (resize/trim avoids ~2x memory).
evidence: drcmda: "It's smaller (~5kb vs 80kb), faster (they say up to 50%)"

title: Dispose of loaders
summary: Request for dispose() on loaders to release Web Workers, WASM, and cached files; discussion of shared WorkerPool between KTX2Loader/DRACOLoader instances.
evidence: body: "loaders that use web workers will leave those threads running in the background" || donmccurdy: "A performance penalty (by not sharing web workers) would catch many by surprise."

title: WebXR always asks for hands support
summary: VRButton always requests the 'hand-tracking' optional feature; reporter claims this may slow JS execution and battery life. Closed for lack of numbers.
evidence: body: "This should only be done if the experience will make use of this feature because it might slow down JavaScript execution." and "I don't have exact numbers."

title: Jank with trivial scrolling animation
ruled_out_findings: Browser compositor/HTML rasterization work causes dropped frames independent of three.js; reproduced with raw WebGL2 and Canvas2D test cases, tracked in crbug.com/1164435
summary: Sporadic frame drops in a simple scrolling animation reproduce with plain WebGL and even Canvas2D/CSS animations across browsers; traced to browser/compositor behavior, not three.js. Closed in favor of the Chromium bug.

title: GLTFLoader: Add an example for `EXT_meshopt_compression`
summary: Request for a GLTFLoader EXT_meshopt_compression example; a later comment notes gltfpack mesh merging reduced draw calls to 2 giving smooth performance.

title: Add per-vertex line width to `LineGeometry` and `LineMaterial`
summary: Request for per-vertex line widths in LineGeometry/LineMaterial; a related prior PR was not merged due to unspecified performance concerns with capsule-intersection based fragment rejection.
evidence: gkjohnson: "that PR uses capsule intersections to determine whether to render the line. Unfortunately it has not been merged due to concerns about performance."

title: DecalGeometry: Decal projections without distortions.
summary: DecalGeometry planar projection distorts/wraps decals around corners. Alternative exponential-map algorithm discussed; noted to have startup distance-calculation cost.
evidence: dipeshdulal: "There are performance impacts during start up as well because of distance calculation that is needed to be done during start up (one time process)."

title: Strict type check on geometry object before accessing key like  isGeometry
summary: Request for null checks on geometry in Box3.expandByObject; declined because argument validation adds per-call cost for correct users.
evidence: donmccurdy: "We do not typically include validation of incorrect inputs to three.js methods, as this creates performance costs paid even by users who are using the APIs correctly."

title: Would Three consider a prototype.reset() function for its value classes (Vectors, Colors, etc)?
summary: Proposal for reset()/default-value introspection on math classes; rejected as an app-level concern. Getter/setter based approach dismissed as too costly for hot properties.
evidence: looeee: "I think getters and setters have too high a performance cost to be used for frequently accessed properties like position and scale." — hedged with "I think", no measurement

title: Raycaster.intersectObjects() recursive flag
summary: Proposal to default Raycaster.intersectObjects recursive flag to true; a user claimed recursive raycasting over large glTF node trees each frame is CPU-costly, which a maintainer disputed.

title: `Object.defineProperty` in `THREE.Vector3` constructor causing a significant performance penalty
summary: Object.defineProperty for isVector3 flags in math class constructors deoptimizes object creation, making Vector3.clone() ~5-10x slower since r120.
evidence: "On my machine, the difference is 5ms (r119) vs 45ms (r120, r125)." plus "replacing `Object.defineProperty( this, 'isVector3', { value: true } );` in `THREE.Vector3` constructor with `this.isVector3 = true;` fixes the issue" || WestLangley: "it causes unnecessary instantiation of objects and garbage-collection"

title: RayCaster: Allow object tests to be more easily extended.
summary: Request to make Raycaster's per-object test extensible; maintainer argues no perf difference vs app-level filtering. No mechanism established.

title: SVG Loader: incorrect rendering in complex SVGs
summary: SVGLoader fails to render complex SVGs (gradients, url refs, paint order). Performance only mentioned as an aside about the reporter's prior Snap.svg implementation.

title: Octree - update specific triangles of object instead of re-adding everything again
summary: Octree only supports fromGraphNode(), forcing full rebuild of all triangles when a single object changes.
evidence: body: "this re-adds all triangles instead of giving the option to only update one object. This can heavily impact performance."

title: SSRPass: throws err for a simple scene.
summary: SSRPass throws when scene mixes InstancedMesh and Mesh due to shared overrideMaterial program; closed as duplicate of #18533.

title: Rework updateWorldMatrix / scene.autoUpdate
summary: Proposal to avoid full scene traversal in updateMatrixWorld via dirty-flag propagation; measurements show several ms per frame spent traversing static scene graphs.
evidence: "timing done in Chrome performance tools" with table rows 5-6 ms vs 2-2.5 ms; "it would not be necessary to always traverse all objects in `scene.updateMatrixWorld`" || "Even in this sample with 7700 objects it should be possible to save 0.5 ms of CPU time on my system"

title: VAO performance issues on Radeon 460
summary: Switching to Vertex Array Objects in r118 caused a large slowdown on several GPUs/browsers; traced to a Chrome (not ANGLE) VAO handling hot spot and fixed upstream in Chrome 93.
evidence: kenrussell: "The problem was solely in Chrome, not ANGLE"; crbug 1192082 quoted as "the best workaround would be to change Three.js back to stop using VAOs."

title: Animations mixing bones that aren't part of their keyframes; can't play two distinct animations at same time
summary: AnimationMixer blends all bones of concurrently played clips; discussion of bone-masking alternatives and their cost.
evidence: RemusMar: "you need to waste a bunch of resources preventing the skin modifier (the weights controller) accessing unwanted vertices"; donmccurdy hedges: "I'm pretty sure that additive blending does not impose any additional per-vertex cost. It may impose an additional per-bone cost"

title: Octree: Memory overload.
summary: Reporter claims Octree.split()'s while+pop loop causes O(n^2) work and memory blowup; maintainers asked for a live demo and closed for lack of info.
evidence: body: "i kinda resolved this issue by using this argument ``--max-old-space-size=4096`` so i dont get this error"

title: Faster PBR Material
summary: Request for a cheaper PBR material; long thread with Quest measurements showing MeshStandardMaterial fragment shading dominates, PMREM atlas sampling cost, and unnecessary background cubemap rendering.
evidence: FrostKiwi: "Percentage Time Shading Fragments                      |           92.67" || Mugen87: "meaning face selection, uv projection, atlas addressing, seam handling, manual trilinear filtering" || davehill00: "I had set a background image (cube map, from a 32-bit EXR) on the scene, which was rendering behind the wall but not contributing anything to the final scene. So that's where all the extra cycles were" || FrostKiwi: "The Quest 3 CPU can't even pull the per-frame Raycasts on 50k Poly meshes without dropping frames hard"

title: npm run test fails on the latest Node.js
summary: Unit test failure on Node 16 caused by global `performance` becoming defined while `self` is not; no performance content.

title: instanceColor attribute is not defined when InstancedMesh is populated asynchronously
summary: instanceColor added asynchronously doesn't trigger shader recompile; maintainer declines per-frame checking citing cost.
evidence: Mugen87: "it would be necessary to check each frame if colors are present or not. For performance reasons, I do not vote to do this"

title: poor performance with some gltf files
summary: GLTFLoader cloned a texture per material/map because of a no-op KHR_texture_transform extension, creating 20 textures from 3, tanking FPS in the editor; worked around in #21821.
evidence: donmccurdy: "so we preemptively clone the texture, but in this case the extension is doing nothing"

title: WebXRManager getCamera()
summary: WebXRManager.getCamera() returns an ArrayCamera whose fov is never computed; maintainer says computing it per frame is avoided for performance.

title: MeshPhysicalMaterial transmission doesn't work correctly in WebXR immersive mode
summary: Transmission broken in WebXR immersive mode; multi-pass render-target approach doesn't handle stereo/AR camera, and transmission is noted as costly for VR.
evidence: "For VR, the performance is very important for better experience. But transmission is costly."

title: Transmission anti aliasing
summary: Objects behind transmissive materials lose anti-aliasing because the transmission render target is not multisampled (WebGL1 limitation); discussion of full-size RT trade-off.
evidence: For the quality, it should be good. But I'm not sure if it's good for the performance.

title: Firefox poor performance / slow rendering: Tracking upstream issue
summary: Meta issue documenting 2.4x-7.5x slower three.js rendering in Firefox on Linux, tracked to upstream Mozilla bug 1010527 about slow WebGL compositing.
evidence: "1010527 - WebGL composites slowly on Linux by default" plus benchmark table showing 4-7x lower FPS in Firefox

title: logarithmicDepthBuffer causes Reflector to be rendered incorrectly
summary: Reflector renders incorrectly with logarithmicDepthBuffer because its shader lacks the logdepthbuf chunks; adding them fixed it.

title: InstancedMesh first two arguments are optional
summary: Debate over making InstancedMesh geometry/material optional; touches on buffer allocation and default Mesh construction costs.
evidence: That'll result in uploading all the data every frame. The gpu doesn't let you expand buffers, you need to upload them again. || drcmda: "these are just empty shells that the GC immediately takes out" || Mugen87: "we've agreed in the past to not do this for performance and code readability reasons"

title: Examples: webgl_loader_gltf_transmission issues
summary: Transmission example issues; incorrect normal passed to refraction function fixed. Discussion establishes cost of depth peeling and of a separate tonemapping pass.
evidence: Mugen87: "Applying gamma and tone mapping in an additional render pass was noticeably slower than doing it inline. In certain examples, performance dropped from 60 to 40 FPS when using a FP32 render target" || is likely to involve rendering the model many times ("depth peeling") so I would expect that to reduce performance

title: WebGLProgram: Make cacheKey human-readable
summary: Request to make WebGLProgram cacheKey human-readable; rejected due to added overhead of maintaining two representations.
evidence: Mugen87: "Having two different representations of the same thing means more code and potentially additional overhead."

title: KTX2 support for threejs.com/editor
summary: KTX2 support in the editor; export requires readable data, and outputting RGBA would lose GPU-compressed texture benefits.

title: WebXR VR Examples are broken since the v130 update on Oculus Quest 2
ruled_out_findings: Switching from XRWebGLLayer to XRWebGLBinding/XRProjectionLayer makes the framebuffer author-created, so the browser's built-in MSAA no longer applies, and EXT_multisampled_render_to_texture is not ex
summary: r130 WebXR layers support broke Quest 2 examples (black screen) and lost antialiasing because XRProjectionLayer framebuffers are app-owned and the multisample extension isn't exposed in WebGL.

title: [Feature request] Add per-instance visibility support to InstanceMesh
summary: Request for per-instance visibility on InstancedMesh; maintainer notes an extra attribute wouldn't help, recommends sorting instances and shrinking count. Later comment reports raycast slowdown from infinity-translation hiding hack.
evidence: Mugen87: "an additional instanced attribute that controls visibility will not improve the performance" ... "you can use the [count]... property to decrease the effective draw range" || bergden: "this hack started causing very severe performance issues when raycasting on the instancedMesh (much worse than when all instances are visible)"

title: FBXLoader: Unable to load animated mesh.
summary: FBXLoader mismatches mesh and bones for a given file; discussion mentions glTF being faster to parse, but no perf mechanism for the bug itself.

title: Updating Chrome browser to v92 from v86 results in very bad performance issue
summary: Chrome 92 causes large FPS drop vs v86 with many InstancedMesh objects; no repro provided, pointed at a Chromium VAO bug.

title: WebGLRenderer: fails to convert CubeCamera renderTarget to PMREM CubeUV format
summary: Render target textures from CubeCamera aren't auto-converted to PMREM CubeUV; regenerating PMREM per frame for dynamic cube cameras is prohibitively expensive, so dynamic env maps with Standard/Physical materials are impractical.
evidence: Mugen87: "Processing dynamic cube maps with `PMREMGenerator` per frame does not work for performance reasons." || elalish: "switch the internal format of CubeUV from RGBE to HalfFloat, which should help performance. I believe the mip-chain alternative to PMREM deleted in #22234 will also work properly, but only with `HalfF"

title: Performance loss revision upgrade r130 -> r131
summary: Reporter measured FPS dropping from 30 to 8-10 between r130 and r131 with 8000 simple cube meshes; no mechanism was ever identified in the thread.

title: Bad performance and stutters on iOS when using lights + shadows
summary: Stutter with lights+shadows on a 7th-gen iPad in Safari; not reproducible on other iPads, attributed to the device/browser and redirected to WebKit without a mechanism.

title: BatchedMesh: Proposal
cause_ids: DCO-01; GBU-06; SGS-03; AS-07; LUU-06; LUU-03; IBL-03; DBD-02; CASI-03
categories: draw_call_overhead; geometry_buffer_updates; scene_graph_scale; animation_skinning; lights_uniforms_ubo; lights_uniforms_ubo; instancing_batching_limits; device_browser_driver; culling_and_spatial_index
strengths: measured; reporter_asserted; speculative; reporter_asserted; speculative; measured; speculative; upstream_bug; reporter_asserted
evidence_kinds: observed_cost; proposed_optimization; hypothetical; proposed_optimization; hypothetical; observed_cost; hypothetical; observed_cost; observed_cost
summary: Proposal for a BatchedMesh API to cut draw-call overhead for many distinct static geometries sharing a material. Discussion covers WEBGL_multi_draw, uniform arrays vs DataTexture/UBO, CPU vertex baking, scene-graph proxy overhead, and culling tradeoffs; prototype measured 40fps vs 30fps. Landed in r159.
evidence: takahirox: "40 fps (BatchedMesh) vs 30 fps (regular Mesh) on my Windows 10 Chrome." || takahirox: "you will no longer need to directly update positions in `setMatrixAt()` in CPU" || donmccurdy: "we're paying the full cost of the scene graph traversal" || gkjohnson: "4 bone weights and 4 bone indices are specified per vertex and the shader has to do 16 texture lookups" || gkjohnson: "mobile limitations (max UBO size, texture fetch performance)" || RenaudRohlinger: "Uniforms Array is by far the worst in performance. FPS drops by 50% or so vs Naive implementation" || gkjohnson: "will add complexity and unnecessary performance overhead" || RenaudRohlinger: "a bug was introduced in the latest version of Safari that reduces this limitation to 256" || vegarringdal: "frustum culling witch is really bad when I merge to much"

title: WebGLRenderer - use alpha: true by default
summary: Request to default WebGLRenderer to alpha:true because MDN/WebGL best practices say alpha:false requires emulating RGB on an RGBA backbuffer; maintainers declined without measurements and noted blending output changes.
evidence: arpu: "Emulating RGB-on-RGBA has real overhead, regardless of implementation approach."

title: Performance problems on Chrome with simple scenes
summary: Low FPS / dropped frames on skinning examples in Chrome; traces showed no three.js hotspot and the same behaviour reproduced in BabylonJS, so the cost lies outside three.js (browser/driver).
evidence: Mugen87: "Especially the long pauses in the second trace look unrelated to `three.js`."

title: Significant slowdown from r0.127.0 to r.0.128.0
summary: App-level slowdown bisected to r128 in a react-three-fiber app; closed for lack of a minimal reproduction, no mechanism identified.

title: WebGLRenderer: Use faster program cache key computation.
ruled_out_findings: console.log in the render path with devtools open, plus profiler-induced deoptimization, inflated the apparent cost of getProgramCacheKey
summary: getProgramCacheKey dominated profiles: it builds an array of strings and joins them, generating garbage, and since r129 (removal of material skinning/vertexTangents flags) it is invoked once or more per mesh per frame via needsProgramChange. Optimized in #22960/#23022; profiler distortion also inflated the original numbers.
evidence: "getProgramCacheKey` takes up close to 20% of the entire time"; "68.5**% of the garbage" || Usnul: "it will cause a lot of heap fragmentation and will make GC pauses longer in general" — asserted by non-maintainer, GC pause effect not measured || gonnavis: "getProgramCacheKeyTime: 0.10 updateMatrixWorldTime: 21.00"

title: SSR Pass only reflection on the floor working in Firefox and chrome
ruled_out_findings: ANGLE/GPU driver miscompiles or mishandles the SSR fragment shader loop, producing black/flickering output; switching ANGLE backend fixes it
summary: SSRPass reflections missing on certain GPU/driver combos; traced to ANGLE/driver shader bug, fixed by driver update or changing ANGLE backend.

title: gltf geometry corrupted on Safari 15
summary: Corrupted glTF geometry on Safari 15 with Radeon Pro GPUs; tracked as a WebKit bug.

title: CSS2DRenderer / CSS3DRenderer: allow usage of existing DOM element
summary: Request to let CSS2D/3DRenderer use an existing DOM element; performance benefit asserted without mechanism.

title: Textures in gLTF sometimes display black, but only on iOS
summary: Textures go black on iOS due to ImageBitmap memory not being freed; workaround is disabling createImageBitmap on iOS.
evidence: donmccurdy: "There seems to be a threshold around 250 MB" and "exactly 10 textures will load, exactly 5 will fail"; niklasramo: "2, 5, 5, 4, 5" || bzztbomb: "you must call `.close` on the `ImageBitmap` instance" ... "The GC of the ImageBitmap isn't enough to free the resources it has (on iOS)."

title: Performance issues between release 125 and 133
summary: Reported 2-3x slowdown between r125 and r133 turned out to be Babel transpiling three.js to ES5, preventing V8 optimisation of updateMatrixWorld/projectObject.
evidence: "Babel transpiles the code onto es5 and performance is 6 times slower. From a renderloop of 5ms to 26fps."

title: Performance drop using correct sRGBEncoding for scene.environment cubemap
summary: Frame hitch when setting sRGBEncoding on an environment cubemap; duplicate of #22631, caused by SRGB8_ALPHA8 texture upload overhead on Windows/Chrome.

title: gl.compile doesn't work for off screen objects
summary: compile() only precompiles shaders, so first-scroll jank came from texture uploads happening lazily on first render.
evidence: Mugen87: "only pre-compiles shaders but does not actually render items. So there are no uniform updates nor texture uploads." — reporter's profile screenshot confirms "it was indeed the texture upload that created lag on first scroll"

title: r133 getProgramInfoLog performance issue
summary: r133 first-frame slowdown attributed to getProgramInfoLog was actually blocking texImage2D for sRGB textures under WebGL2 (#22631).

title: Geometry shaders
summary: Request for mesh/geometry shaders for automatic LOD; not possible in WebGL/WebGPU.

title: CurvePath getLengths() not updating
summary: CurvePath.updateArcLengths() doesn't recurse into child curves by design; recursing would be too expensive. Resolved as documentation clarification.
evidence: Mugen87: "Hence it has to update all of them which is bad for performance."

title: 10x shader compilation time regression from r132 to r133 (Windows)
summary: Switching sRGB textures to SRGB8_ALPHA8 internal format in r133 triggered a driver/browser pathological path on Windows, making texture upload/mipmap generation (surfacing as long getProgramInfoLog/gl call stalls) ~10x slower. Fixed by reverting SRGB8_ALPHA8 usage (#22759) pending Chromium bug 1256340.
evidence: "Then load times are instantly better (though the scene is predictably washed out.)" plus profiles showing ~500ms vs ~5 seconds

title: WebGL2: Asynchronous Readback with PIXEL_PACK_BUFFERs
summary: Request for asynchronous readback via PIXEL_PACK_BUFFER because readRenderTargetPixels forces a GPU sync stall costing tens of ms per call.
evidence: body: "waits for a sync with the GPU before the download starts, costing tens of milliseconds per-call"

title: Extremely slow performance with specific file
summary: Asset with many materials sharing one sRGB texture hangs the browser; closed as duplicate of #22758 (SRGB8_ALPHA8 + repeated texture upload per material).

title: generateUUID() is slow after the introduction of crypto.randomUUID()
summary: MathUtils.generateUUID switched to crypto.randomUUID(), which is ~97% slower in benchmarks and dominated object creation during parsing; change was reverted.
evidence: body: "we're seing `generateUUID()` being a significant factor (20-40%) of the time setting up ThreeJS Meshes" plus jsbench link showing "97% slower"; Mugen87: "Since `crypto.randomUUID()` is actually that much slower, it's probably better to revert."

title: Unmuting video's causing performance issues on iOS
summary: Video textures stutter on iOS Safari after unmuting; redirected to WebKit bug tracker with no mechanism identified.

title: ArcballControls is using .clone() unnecessarily
summary: ArcballControls allocates new objects via .clone() and returns new objects from helper methods on every mouse move, violating three.js reuse convention; refactor abandoned as too risky.
evidence: Mugen87: "certain methods like `calculateRotationAxis()` or `getCursorNDC()` return new objects"; WestLangley: "Every time the mouse moves."

title: Critical performance issue even though scene doesn't have a lot of objects.
summary: Reporter saw render() take 500-600ms when one extra cabinet object was added; closed by reporter because the repro didn't work, no mechanism identified.

title: Adding GLSL style swizzling to vectors
summary: Proposal for GLSL-style swizzle getters on vectors rejected partly because each getter must allocate a new Vector instance per access.
evidence: Mugen87: "You also allocate a new vector instance in your getters at every call which is a no-go in context of performance."

title: Enable usage of SRGB8_ALPHA8
summary: Tracking issue to re-enable SRGB8_ALPHA8 once the Chromium sRGB decode performance bug is fixed or texStorage2D is adopted.
evidence: "performance issues while decoding sRGB textures under Windows" linked to Chromium Issue 1256340

evidence: "RGBA8 ->47 FPS" ... "FP16 -> 45 FPS" ... "FP32 -> 39 FPS"; "Examples that used to run at 60 FPS on my iMac now run at approx. 40 FPS." || bhouston: "many mobile devices simply didn't have enough memory to handle it properly" and "Just using that much memory could slow things down a lot, even without considering the separate pass."

title: MorphTargets - morphTargetInfluences in Safari not transforming mesh object
summary: Morph target influences render incorrectly in Safari on Intel Macs; traced to a Safari/driver bug, triggered by antialias:true context. No performance content.

title: Performance Regression: `getProgram` & `getProgramCacheKey` been called too many times.
summary: getProgram/getProgramCacheKey called many more times per frame in r135 vs r129; closed as duplicate of #22530.

title: webgl_instancing_performance naive performs better
summary: In the instancing_performance example the naive path outran instancing on macOS Chrome; attributed to a known Chromium mac bug (crbug.com/1245448).
evidence: Mugen87: "The Chromium issue states this happens only on mac."

title: outputEncoding not handled correctly when using sRGB render target in WebGL2
summary: sRGB render targets got double-encoded (inline shader encode plus hardware); side discussion on the cost of repeated sRGB encode/decode and half-float buffers in FX chains.
evidence: Mugen87: "This encoding/decoding overhead is waste from my point of view." || vanruesc: "it requires `HalfFloatType` buffers to avoid banding which can have an impact on performance"

title: Setting Material.blending to "CustomBlending" no longer works blends as expected
summary: CustomBlending with opacity broke in r137 due to #23361 forcing gl_FragColor.a = 1.0 for non-transparent materials; that change existed because always using an RGBA default framebuffer (alpha:true) avoids browser emulation of alpha:false, a large perf win.
evidence: mrdoob: "apparently many systems do not create a webgl context with `alpha: false` so the browser has to emulate it"; Mugen87: "always having a RGBA default framebuffer introduced the performance benefit" || gkjohnson: "my understanding is that theres a performance impact when enabling blending"

title: Any PolyhedronGeometry tanks the GPU
summary: Reporter sees ~5FPS with PolyhedronGeometry-based InstancedMesh on Chrome/2016 MacBook only; closed for lack of a minimal reproduction, no mechanism identified.

title: WebGL2 asynchronous readback implementation.
summary: Request for WebGL2 async readback (PIXEL_PACK_BUFFER + fences) because blocking gl.readPixels stalls the pipeline; closed as duplicate of #22779.

title: Multisampling effectively disables Depth Texture
summary: Depth texture empty on multisampled render targets because depth is invalidated during the multisample blit—an intentional WebXR performance optimization whose opt-out flag was lost in r138.

title: Roadmap for a color-managed workflow in three.js
summary: Roadmap tracking issue for color-managed workflow. Performance is only mentioned in passing: applying the sRGB OETF in a separate render target pass is described as costly.
evidence: "Currently we have the option of applying the OETF in a render target (which is costly), or at the end of each fragment shader during initial rendering"

title: Unstable shadows since r138
summary: Shadows became unstable (and a perf regression in skinning example appeared) after r138; bisected to PR #23559, reverting fixes both, but no explanation of the mechanism.
evidence: Mugen87: "I've also noticed a performance regression in `webgl_animation_skinning_blending` on my iMac. Reverting the PR solves this issue, too."

title: Implement Bounding Boxes in Groups to improve the frustum culling performance.
summary: Request for hierarchical bounding volumes on Group so frustum culling can skip whole subtrees; maintainer declined, suggesting app-level BVH/spatial structures.
evidence: "if you have a scene with 100 groups of 10 meshes each, with the actual way there are performed a 1000 of checks"

title: After calling WebGLRenderer.resetState() subsequent render does not setup VertexAttributes
summary: resetState() doesn't reset cached vertex attribute state when sharing a WebGL context; the only workaround (recreating scene each frame) is noted as bad for performance.

title: Wierd behaviour of single MorphTarget.position record on large buffer geometry

title: Reconsider removal of inline sRGB decode

evidence: body: "or a costly CPU-side conversion if not" || tangobravo: "it wouldn't surprise me if many browsers only have a hardware fast path implemented for RGBA formats"

title: WebGL1Renderer now faster than WebGLRenderer after browser update

title: Check exist image in texture before export
summary: Request for null-image validation checks in texture export; declined partly citing performance/readability cost of validation code.

title: OBJExporter (also PLY and STL): Support for deformable meshes (skins & morphs)

title: new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 0).angleTo(new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 0)) should be undefined

title: Making 'three' tree-shakeable
cause_ids: BSLT-01; O-12; BSLT-03; BSLT-05; SPC-14; BSLT-02
categories: bundle_size_load_time; other; bundle_size_load_time; bundle_size_load_time; shader_program_compilation; bundle_size_load_time
strengths: reporter_asserted; speculative; maintainer_confirmed; maintainer_confirmed; reporter_asserted; maintainer_confirmed
evidence_kinds: observed_cost; hypothetical; observed_cost; observed_cost; observed_cost; observed_cost
summary: Long thread on making the 'three' npm package tree-shakeable. Contributors enumerate concrete module-level side effects (ShaderLib/UniformsLib object literals, MathUtils _lut loop, DataUtils tables, ObjectLoader Geometries namespace, Material.fromType, Materials.js re-exports, static class properties and .prototype.* assignments outside class bodies, __THREE_DEVTOOLS__/window.__THREE__ globals) that force bundlers to retain the entire dependency graph, inflating bundle size (~420kb-1MB) and load-time evaluation. Also documented: `instanceof` defeats tree-shaking (hence .isFoo flags), webpack cannot tree-shake static class properties, and a flat bundle has no module boundaries so `sideEffects: false` barely helps. Largely closed as wontfix/workaround since splitting the ShaderChunk `#include <...>` namespace would be a huge breaking change.
evidence: pschroen: "`ShaderLib.js`, `UniformsLib.js` and `ShaderChunk.js` are also side-effects" || pschroen: "I'd imagine this would improve load time, and also reduce memory usage a little as well." || marcofugaro: "Yup, it will be included. This is the reason three switched to `.is*`" || marcofugaro: "Webpack has no support for tree-shaking static class properties" || pschroen: "the entire shader system of three.js is built around these [includes]" || lukastaegert: "It just does not make a lot of difference for a flat bundle. As soon as you import anything, all side effects are included."
